example.gloss: This time tomorrow I'll be on the train. I'll probably be sleeping.

items.note: No such tense. Present with a time frame; 'am' plus infinitive only when the mid-action sense is the point.

items.target: scho + duration + Perfekt (+ gha/gsi)

example.target: Ich ha scho es Jahr dete gschaffet gha, wo d Firma zuegmacht hät.
example.gloss: I'd been working there for a year when the firm closed.

items.note: Duration with 'scho' plus doubled Perfekt (gschaffet gha) marks 'had been doing'. In fast speech the second 'gha' is often dropped.

items.target: wänn ___ hett/wär + Partizip, hett/wär ___ + Partizip

example.target: Wänn ich das gwüsst hett, wär ich nöd cho.
example.gloss: If I'd known that, I wouldn't have come.

items.note: Both clauses use 'hett' or 'wär' plus participle; no 'würd' in the past. Standard 'hätte/wäre' forms map one to one.

items.target: wänn ___ hett + Partizip, würd/wär ich jetzt ___

example.target: Wänn ich de Job gno hett, wär ich jetzt z Gänf.
example.gloss: If I'd taken the job, I'd be in Geneva now.

items.note: Past condition with 'hett/wär' plus participle, present result with 'wär/würd' plus 'jetzt'. 'jetzt' is what signals the mix.

items.target: wird / isch worde + Partizip; überchoo + Partizip (get-passive)

example.target: Das wird gmacht. Das isch gmacht worde. Ich ha s Päckli gliferet überchoo.
example.gloss: That's being done. That was done. I got the parcel delivered.

items.note: Same building blocks as Standard German, but everyday speech converts to 'me' (me hät s gmacht). The dative get-passive uses 'überchoo' (to receive), never 'kriegen'.

items.target: aber / trotzdem / allerdings

example.target: S Wätter isch schlächt gsi. Trotzdem simmer go wandere. Allerdings nöd lang.
example.gloss: The weather was bad. Nevertheless we went hiking. Though not for long.

items.note: 'trotzdem' in first position, verb next. 'allerdings' adds a caveat; 'jedoch' is written Standard German and sounds stiff in dialect.

items.target: trotz ___ (dative) / trotzdem, dass ___

example.target: Trotz em Räge simmer go laufe. Trotzdem, dass er chrank isch, chunt er.
example.gloss: Despite the rain we went walking. Even though he's ill, he's coming.

items.note: 'trotz' takes the dative in dialect (trotz em Räge), not the genitive of Standard German. 'trotzdem, dass' as a conjunction is spoken, 'obwohl' is neater.

items.target: während ___ / ___, ___ dagäge ___

example.target: Während d Miete stiiged, bliibed d Löhn gliich.
example.gloss: Whereas rents rise, salaries stay the same.

items.note: 'während' with contrast meaning is verb-final and slightly formal. Two main clauses with 'dagäge' or 'hingäge' after the subject are the spoken alternative.

items.target: uf de eine Siite ___, uf de andere ___ / einersiits, anderersiits
items.gloss: on the one hand ___, on the other hand ___

example.target: Uf de eine Siite isch s praktisch, uf de andere Siite isch s tüür.
example.gloss: On the one hand it's practical, on the other hand it's expensive.

items.note: Both halves take first position: verb straight after 'Siite'. 'einersiits/anderersiits' is the shorter, slightly more formal pair.

items.target: usser ___ (verb-final) / wänn ___ nöd

example.target: Ich chume, usser es rägnet. Wänn s nöd rägnet, chume ich.
example.gloss: I'll come, unless it rains. If it doesn't rain, I'll come.

items.note: 'usser' (Standard 'außer') as a conjunction keeps main-clause order in speech ('usser es rägnet'); 'usser wänn' is also common. 'es sei denn' is written.

items.target: solang ___ (verb-final) / vorusgsetzt, dass ___

example.target: Du chasch bliibe, solang du ruhig bisch. Vorusgsetzt, dass s Wätter mitmacht.
example.gloss: You can stay as long as you're quiet. Provided the weather plays along.

items.note: 'solang' is verb-final. 'vorusgsetzt, dass' is the formal condition; in speech 'wänn' with a stressed 'aber' does the same job.

items.target: falls ___ (verb-final) / für de Fall, dass ___

example.target: Nimm en Schirm mit, falls es rägnet.
example.gloss: Take an umbrella in case it rains.

items.note: 'falls' covers 'if' and 'in case'; verb at the end. 'zur Sicherheit' (to be safe) is the adverb that adds the precaution sense.

items.target: wär au immer / was au immer / egal wo

example.target: Egal wo du bisch, ich chume. Was au immer passiert, mir mached wiiter.
example.gloss: Wherever you are, I'll come. Whatever happens, we carry on.

items.note: 'egal' plus question word (egal wär, egal was, egal wo) is the spoken form; 'was au immer' is closer to Standard 'was auch immer'. Verb-final in the clause.

items.target: nöd nu ___, sondern au ___

example.target: Er redt nöd nu Dütsch, sondern au Französisch und Italienisch.
example.gloss: He speaks not only German but also French and Italian.

items.note: 'nu' (Standard 'nur'). 'sondern' survives here after a negative; plain 'aber' would be wrong. No inversion in the second half.

items.target: au wänn ___ (verb-final)

example.target: Au wänn s rägnet, gang ich go laufe.
example.gloss: Even if it rains, I'm going for a walk.

items.note: 'au wänn' also covers 'even though' in dialect ('obwohl' is the alternative). Verb-final, then main clause starts with its verb.

items.target: de/d/s with abstract nouns; plural generic without article
items.gloss: Articles with abstract and generic nouns

example.target: D Ziit isch Gäld. Ich ha d Musig gern. Chind bruuched Schlaaf.
example.gloss: Time is money. I like music. Children need sleep.

items.note: Abstract nouns usually take the article (d Ziit, s Läbe, d Liebi) more than in English; bare plurals are generic (Chind, Lüüt). Same rule as Standard German.

items.target: jede / jedi / jedes, alli, beidi, keine vo beidne, ein vo beidne
items.gloss: each, every, all, both, neither, either

example.target: Jede Tag, jedi Wuche, jedes Jahr. Alli sind cho, beidi Brüedere au.
example.gloss: Every day, every week, every year. Everyone came, both brothers too.

items.note: 'jede' agrees like an adjective (jede/jedi/jedes). 'beidi' for both; 'either/neither of the two' is phrased as 'ein/keine vo beidne'.

items.target: e Frag stelle, e Entscheidig träffe, Sinn mache, sich Müe gää
items.gloss: ask a question, make a decision, make sense, make an effort

example.target: Ich ha e Frag. Mir müend e Entscheidig träffe. Das macht Sinn.
example.gloss: I have a question. We have to make a decision. That makes sense.

items.note: Mostly Standard German collocations in dialect dress. Watch 'Sinn mache' (now accepted), 'es Foti mache' (take a photo), 'Feierabend mache' (knock off work).

items.target: separable prefixes: aa-, ab-, uuf-, ii-, uus-, mit-, zue-, hei-

example.target: Ich lüüte dir aa. Ich stah am Sächsi uuf. Chunsch mit?
example.gloss: I'll call you. I get up at six. Coming along?

items.note: Prefix goes to the end in main clauses, rejoins in subordinate clauses and in the participle: aaglüütet, uufgstande. 'z' slips inside: uufzstaa.

items.target: d Freiheit (freedom), d Sicherheit (security), d Gerächtigkeit (justice), d Verantwortig (responsibility), d Erfahrig (experience), d Möglichkeit (possibility), de Vorteil (advantage), de Nachteil (disadvantage), s Risiko (risk), d Folg (consequence), d Lösig (solution), d Entwicklig (development), de Unterschid (difference), de Zämehang (connection), d Uusnahm (exception), d Bedütig (meaning)
items.note: Endings -ung becomes -ig (Erfahrig, Lösig, Entwicklig), -keit stays. Most of this vocabulary is shared with Standard German; in a real debate Swiss often slide into Standard forms.

items.target: d Firma (company), s Gschäft (business/shop), de Kund (customer), d Kundin (customer f.), s Aagebot (offer), de Vertrag (contract), d Rächnig (invoice), de Termin (appointment), d Sitzig (meeting), verhandle (negotiate), d Frischt (deadline), liefere (deliver), d Liferig (delivery), de Umsatz (turnover), de Gwünn (profit), d Kündigung (termination), d KMU (SMEs)
items.note: 'Frischt' (Standard 'Frist') is a deadline; 'Termin' an appointment. 'Rächnig' is both the invoice and the bill. Business emails are always Standard German.

items.target: d Politik (politics), d Abstimmig (referendum vote), abstimme (to vote on an issue), d Wahle (elections), d Initiativ (popular initiative), d Regierig (government), de Bundesrat (Federal Council), d Gmeind (municipality), de Kanton (canton), s Gsetz (law), d Gsellschaft (society), d Wirtschaft (economy), d Uuslände (foreigners), d Iiwanderig (immigration), d Nachrichte (news), d Meinigsfreiheit (free speech)
items.note: Direct democracy shapes the vocabulary: 'abstimme' four times a year, 'd Initiativ', 'd Gmeind'. 'Bundesrat' is the seven-person government, not a chamber.

items.target: d Wüsseschaft (science), d Forschig (research), d ETH (federal tech university), s Experimänt (experiment), d Technik (technology), d Energie (energy), de Strom (electricity), d Chärnchraft (nuclear power), d Sunneenergie (solar), d Medizin (medicine), d Impfig (vaccination), d KI (AI), d Date (data), entwickle (develop), erfinde (invent), s Ergäbnis (result)
items.note: 'Forschig' and 'Impfig' show -ung to -ig. 'd KI' (künschtlichi Intelligänz) is the AI acronym. Technical talk often switches to Standard German or English terms.

items.target: d Kunscht (art), s Museum (museum), s Theater (theatre), s Kino (cinema), de Film (film), s Buech (book), läse (read), d Musig (music), s Konzärt (concert), d Band (band), s Fescht (festival/party), d Fasnacht (carnival), s Sächsilüüte (Zürich spring festival), de Böögg (its snowman), s Bild (picture), male (paint), d Uusstellig (exhibition), zeichne (draw)
items.note: 'Fescht' is any party or festival. Zürich culture words: Sächsilüüte with the Böögg, Street Parade, Züri Fäscht. 'Musig' has a hard g.

items.target: Zürich vs Bern vs Basel vs Wallis: vowels, 'ich', 'not', tempo
items.note: Bern: slow, 'ig' for ich, 'nid', 'u' for und, l becomes u (Miuch for Milch). Basel: 'nit', unrounded vowels (Bieb for Büeb), 'e' for ä. Wallis and Graubünden are hardest; Zürich is fast and 'nöd'.

items.target: Doubt: rising 'ja?'; sarcasm: flat 'jaja'; enthusiasm: stretched 'mega', 'uu'
items.note: 'jaja' said flat means 'yeah right' or 'shut up'; 'jaa' stretched means 'I know'. Enthusiasm lengthens the stressed vowel (meeega guet). The particle 'gäll' seeks agreement warmly.

items.target: Me chönnt säge, dass ___ / Me chönnt argumentiere, ___
items.gloss: One could say that ___ / One could argue ___

example.target: Me chönnt säge, dass Homeoffice d Produktivität steigeret.
example.gloss: One could argue that working from home raises productivity.

items.note: 'me chönnt' (one could) replaces the English passive. 'dass' sends the verb to the end; dropping 'dass' is fine in speech.

items.target: Zuegää, ___ / Klar, ___ / Es stimmt scho, ___

example.target: Zuegää, s choscht meh. Aber uf d Dauer lohnt sichs.
example.gloss: Admittedly, it costs more. But in the long run it pays off.

items.note: 'Zuegää' is the participle of zuegää (admit), used like 'zugegeben'. In casual talk 'klar' or 'scho' does the same job.

items.target: Trotzdem, ___ / Aber äbe, ___ / Anderersiits ___
items.gloss: That said, ___ / But then again, ___ / On the other hand ___

example.target: S Angebot isch guet. Aber äbe, mir händ s Gäld nöd.
example.gloss: The offer is good. That said, we don't have the money.

items.note: 'Aber äbe' (äbe = eben, 'that's the thing') is the Swiss way to swing back after a concession. 'trotzdem' in first position takes the verb next.

items.target: Churz gseit, ___ / Zämegfasst ___ / Unter em Strich ___
items.gloss: In short, ___ / To sum up ___ / Bottom line ___

example.target: Churz gseit: es isch z tüür und z langsam.
example.gloss: In short: it's too expensive and too slow.

items.note: 'Churz gseit' (shortly said) with a colon or comma, then a main clause. 'Unter em Strich' (below the line) is the bottom-line phrase.

items.target: Ich verstaa din Punkt, aber ___ / Das isch en guete Punkt, aber ___
items.gloss: I take your point, but ___ / That's a good point, but ___

example.target: Ich verstaa din Punkt, aber ich gseh das anders.
example.gloss: I take your point, but I see it differently.

items.note: 'din Punkt' (your point) is an anglicism people really use. 'gseh' (see) is the participle and present at once.

items.target: Wär s okay, wänn ___? / Machts dir öppis uus, wänn ___?
items.gloss: Would it be okay if ___? / Does it bother you if ___?

example.target: Machts dir öppis uus, wänn ich s Fänschter uufmache?
example.gloss: Would you mind if I open the window?

items.note: No -ing: 'wänn' clause, verb-final. 'öppis uusmache' (Standard 'etwas ausmachen') is the 'mind' verb; formal: 'Machts Ine öppis uus'.

items.target: Ich ha mich gfragt, öb du ___ chöntsch / Wär s möglich, ___?
items.gloss: I was wondering if you could ___ / Would it be possible to ___?

example.target: Ich ha mich gfragt, öb du mer villicht hälfe chöntsch.
example.gloss: I was wondering if you could maybe help me.

items.note: 'öb' (whether) clause with 'chöntsch' at the end. In formal writing it becomes Standard 'Ich wäre Ihnen dankbar, wenn Sie ...'.

items.target: Alles in allem ___ / Unter em Strich ___ / Im Grosse und Ganze ___
items.gloss: On balance ___ / All in all ___ / On the whole ___

example.target: Alles in allem find ich s e gueti Lösig.
example.gloss: On balance I think it's a good solution.

items.note: All three take first position, so the verb comes next (find ich). 'Unter em Strich' is the most colloquial.

items.target: Das stimmt, sowiit ___ / Das gilt nu, wänn ___
items.gloss: That's true insofar as ___ / That only holds if ___

example.target: Das stimmt bis zu eme gwüsse Grad, aber s gilt nu, wänn d Qualität kei Rolle spilt.
example.gloss: That's true up to a point, but it only holds if quality doesn't matter.

items.note: Uses D-ARGUABLE, G-INSOFAR, G-NEVERTHELESS. Precision in dialect comes from 'nu wänn', 'sowiit', 'bis zu eme gwüsse Grad' rather than formal syntax.

items.target: dialect du / dialect Sie / Standard German written
items.gloss: casual / neutral / formal versions of one request

example.target: Chasch mer s schicke? / Chönted Si mer das schicke? / Könnten Sie mir das bitte zusenden?
example.gloss: Can you send me that? / Could you send me that? / Could you kindly send that to me?

items.note: Uses T-REGISTER, L-REGISTER-PAIRS. The formal end of the scale is not formal dialect but Standard German: register shift in Switzerland is partly a language shift.

items.target: Super, ___ / Das isch ja toll / Na bravo / nöd grad ___
items.gloss: Great, ___ / That's just wonderful / Well done / not exactly ___

example.target: Super, de Zug isch wieder z spaat. Das isch ja toll. Nöd grad, was ich bruuche.
example.gloss: Great, the train's late again. Just wonderful. Not exactly what I need.

items.note: Uses P-IRONY-TONE, C-PUT-IT-MILDLY, D-SO-MUCH-FOR. Irony is carried by flat tone plus 'ja' and 'grad'; Swiss understatement is 'nöd schlächt' for 'excellent'.

items.target: Fönd mer aa / Chömmer zum nächschte Punkt? / Zämegfasst: ___
items.gloss: Let's start / Can we move to the next point? / To sum up: ___

example.target: Guet, fönd mer aa. Sorry, chömmer das spöter aaluege? Zämegfasst: mir mached s so.
example.gloss: Right, let's start. Sorry, can we look at that later? To sum up: we'll do it this way.

items.note: Uses C-IF-I-MAY, C-MOVE-ON, G-GIVEN-THAT. 'fönd mer aa' (aafange) and 'chömmer' (chönd mir) are the chairing clitics; Swiss meetings run in dialect unless a non-Swiss is present.

items.target: Ich bi nöd ganz sicher, öb ___ / Ich hett eher erwartet, dass ___
items.gloss: I'm not entirely sure whether ___ / I'd rather have expected that ___

example.target: Ich bi nöd ganz sicher, öb das so gaat. Ich hett eher erwartet, dass mir zerscht teschted.
example.gloss: I'm not entirely sure that works. I'd rather have expected us to test first.

items.note: Uses C-WITH-RESPECT, D-WOULD-HAVE-THOUGHT, G-ALBEIT. Criticism arrives as doubt about oneself ('ich bi nöd sicher') plus a question; direct 'das isch falsch' is rare.

items.target: Mir bestönd druf, dass ___ / Süscht müend mir ___
items.gloss: We insist that ___ / Otherwise we'll have to ___

example.target: Mir bestönd druf, dass Si pünktlich lifered. Süscht müend mir de Vertrag nöi aaluege.
example.gloss: We insist that you deliver on time. Otherwise we'll have to review the contract.

items.note: Uses D-SUBJUNCTIVE, G-PROVIDED, D-HAD-I-KNOWN. Real negotiations with a Swiss supplier happen in dialect with Sie; the written follow-up is Standard German.

items.target: Defür spricht ___, dagäge ___ / Entscheidend isch, ___
items.gloss: In favour is ___, against ___ / The decisive thing is ___

example.target: Defür spricht de Priis, dagäge d Qualität. Entscheidend isch, wie lang s halte mues.
example.gloss: The price argues for it, the quality against. What's decisive is how long it must last.

items.note: Uses G-HENCE, C-ALL-THINGS, G-OTHER-HAND. 'Defür spricht' / 'dagäge spricht' are the weighing verbs; 'entscheidend isch' takes a wie/öb clause.

items.target: Ich hett dänkt, ___ / Ich hett eher erwartet, dass ___
items.gloss: I would have thought ___ / I'd rather have expected that ___

example.target: Ich hett dänkt, mir teschted das zerscht.
example.gloss: I'd have thought we'd test that first.

items.note: 'hett dänkt' (Standard 'hätte gedacht') with a dass-less clause is the softest disagreement. Add 'ehrlich gseit' to sharpen it slightly.

items.target: Me cha scho säge, dass ___ / Es spricht einiges defür, dass ___
items.gloss: One could well say that ___ / There's a fair case that ___

example.target: Es spricht einiges defür, dass KI vil Übersetzige übernimmt.
example.gloss: There's a fair case that AI will take over many translations.

items.note: Formal 'es isch umstritte' exists but 'me cha scho säge' and 'es spricht einiges defür' are how people actually hedge a claim. 'defür' = dafür.

items.target: dänn cha ich grad au ___ / das cha guet ___
items.gloss: then I may as well ___ / that may well ___

example.target: Wänn ich scho daa bi, cha ich grad au poschte. Das cha guet en Monet gaa.
example.gloss: Since I'm here anyway, I may as well shop. That may well take a month.

items.note: 'grad au' (right away too) after 'cha' gives 'might as well'. 'cha guet' (can well) plus infinitive is 'may well'; both use plain 'cha'.

items.target: si behauptet, si heig ___ / es gseht so uus, als hett si ___
items.gloss: she claims to have ___ / it looks as if she had ___

example.target: Si behauptet, si heig s nöd gwüsst. Es gseht so uus, als hett er alles vergässe.
example.gloss: She claims not to have known. It looks as if he's forgotten everything.

items.note: No perfect infinitive: use a clause. 'heig' is the Zürich reportive for 'hät' after verbs of saying; 'als hett/wär' after 'es gseht so uus'.

items.target: ich finde s scho ___ / ich ha s würkli probiert / doch, ___
items.gloss: I do think it's ___ / I really did try / yes I do

example.target: Ich finde s scho wichtig. Ich ha s würkli probiert. — Du häsch nöd! — Doch!
example.gloss: I do think it's important. I really did try. — You didn't! — I did!

items.note: No emphatic auxiliary: stress plus 'scho', 'würkli', 'sehr wohl'. 'Doch' contradicts a negative in one word, as in Standard German.

items.target: Hett ich das gwüsst, ___ / Sött das nöd chlappe, ___
items.gloss: Had I known, ___ / Should that not work, ___

example.target: Hett ich das gwüsst, wär ich nöd cho. Sött das nöd chlappe, mälded Si sich.
example.gloss: Had I known, I wouldn't have come. Should that not work, get in touch.

items.note: Verb-first conditionals work in dialect: hett ich, wär ich, sött das. They are less bookish than in English and common in speech.

items.target: ich bestah druf, dass ___ (present) / es isch wichtig, dass ___
items.gloss: I insist that ___ / it is vital that ___

example.target: Ich bestah druf, dass er pünktlich chunt. Es isch wichtig, dass si das wüssed.
example.gloss: I insist that he come on time. It's vital that they know.

items.note: No subjunctive after these verbs: plain present in a dass-clause, verb at the end. 'söll' is added for a demand on a third party (dass er söll cho).

items.target: ich hett eigentli ___ sölle / es wär ___ gsi
items.gloss: I was to have ___ / it was going to be ___

example.target: Ich hett eigentli am Mäntig fliege sölle. Es wär mini erschti Reis gsi.
example.gloss: I was to have flown on Monday. It would have been my first trip.

items.note: 'hett eigentli ... sölle' (eigentli = actually, originally) is the future-in-the-past. 'wär ... gsi' for what would have been.

items.target: Nachdem ich ___ (Perfekt), ___ / Wo ich ___ gha ha, ___
items.gloss: Having ___, I ___ / When I had ___, I ___

example.target: Nachdem ich s Projäkt abgschlosse gha ha, han ich ghört, dass sich alles gänderet hät.
example.gloss: Having finished the project, I heard that everything had changed.

items.note: Participle clauses do not exist in dialect: use 'nachdem' or 'wo' with the (doubled) Perfekt, verb-final. Then main clause with verb first.

items.target: Ich ha kei Ahnig gha, dass ___ / Ich hett nie dänkt, dass ___
items.gloss: I had no idea that ___ / I'd never have thought that ___

example.target: Ich ha kei Ahnig gha, dass de Flug scho gstriche gsi isch.
example.gloss: Little did I know the flight had already been cancelled.

items.note: No negative inversion: 'kei Ahnig gha' (had no idea) or 'nie dänkt' with a dass-clause. 'Far from being' is 'alles anderi als' (anything but).

items.target: Das wärs gsi mit ___ / So vil zu ___ / Vergiss ___

example.target: Das wärs gsi mit de Ferie. So vil zum Plan.
example.gloss: So much for the holidays. So much for the plan.

items.note: 'Das wärs gsi mit' (that would have been it with) plus dative is the ironic version; 'so vil zu' is the flatter one. 'Vergiss es' = never mind.

items.target: Chuum ha ich ___, isch ___ / Ich ha grad ___, da ___
items.gloss: Hardly had I ___ when ___ / I had just ___ when ___

example.target: Chuum han ich de Bricht abgschickt, isch d Mail vom Kund cho.
example.gloss: No sooner had I sent the report than the client's mail came.

items.note: 'Chuum' (hardly) in first position gives the inversion for free (chuum han ich). No 'als/than': the second clause just follows, verb first.

items.target: dialect du / dialect Si / Swiss Standard German for writing

example.target: Chunsch? / Chömed Si? / Kommen Sie? — Gib mer das / Gänd Si mer das bitte.
example.gloss: You coming? / Are you coming? / (written) — Give me that / Please give me that (Sie).

items.note: The formal register of a Swiss German speaker is Standard German, spoken with a Swiss accent and 'ss' for ß. Within dialect, Sie plus 'chönted' plus 'bitte' is as formal as it gets.

items.target: not applicable: dass-clause with Perfekt / 'als hett + Partizip'

example.target: Er behauptet, dass er s gmacht hät. Es gseht so uus, als hett er s vergässe.
example.gloss: He claims to have done it. He seems to have forgotten.

items.note: There is no 'to have done' infinitive; 'gmacht z haa' is possible but stilted. Rephrase as a clause after behaupte, schiine, säge.

items.target: time or negative adverb first, verb second: chuum, nie, nu, erscht

example.target: Nie hett ich das dänkt. Erscht dänn han ich s gmerkt.
example.gloss: Never would I have thought that. Only then did I notice.

items.note: Verb-second does this automatically: any fronted adverb puts the verb next. It is emphasis by fronting, not a special negative pattern.

items.target: n/a: Konjunktiv II (wär, hett, würd) only; reportive heig/sig optional

example.target: Ich wett, er wär daa. Si hät gseit, si sig chrank. Wichtig isch, dass er chunt.
example.gloss: I wish he were here. She said she was ill. It's important that he come.

items.note: Konjunktiv II lives (wär, hett, chönnt, würd). Zürich also keeps a reportive Konjunktiv I (sig, heig, chömi) after verbs of saying, unlike most German speech, but present after 'wichtig, dass'.

items.target: hett ___ sölle / hett ___ wele / wär ___ gsi

example.target: Ich hett am Mäntig aafange sölle, aber dänn bin ich chrank worde.
example.gloss: I was going to start on Monday, but then I fell ill.

items.note: 'hett ... sölle/wele' (was supposed/going to) with the modal at the very end; 'eigentli' makes the thwarted plan explicit.

items.target: trotzdem / gliichwohl / dänn doch

example.target: Es isch tüür gsi. Trotzdem hämmer s gmacht. Es hät sich dänn doch glohnt.
example.gloss: It was expensive. Nevertheless we did it. It was worth it after all.

items.note: 'trotzdem' does all the work in dialect ('dennoch' is written). 'gliichwohl' is heard from older speakers; 'dänn doch' adds 'in the end anyway'.

items.target: wänn au ___ / zwar ___, aber ___ / au wänn nu ___
items.gloss: albeit / admittedly ___ but / even if only ___

example.target: De Plan isch guet, wänn au e chli riskant. Es isch zwar chli, aber fein.
example.gloss: The plan is good, albeit a bit risky. It's small, admittedly, but nice.

items.note: No one-word 'albeit': 'wänn au' plus an adjective or 'zwar ... aber'. The 'wänn au' tag can hang after a comma without a verb.

items.target: sowiit ___ / insofärn, als ___ / i dem Sinn, dass ___
items.gloss: insofar as / to the extent that / in the sense that

example.target: Das stimmt sowiit, als s um Standardtext gaat.
example.gloss: That holds insofar as it concerns standard text.

items.note: 'sowiit' (Standard 'soweit') plus 'als' clause, verb-final. Colloquial: 'das stimmt scho, aber nu bi'. 'insofärn' marks academic register.

items.target: wil ___ ja ___ / aagsichts vo ___ / wo mer doch ___
items.gloss: given that ___ / in view of ___ / since after all we ___

example.target: Wo mer doch nu no zää Minute händ, mache mer wiiter. Aagsichts vo de Ziit chürze mer ab.
example.gloss: Given we've only ten minutes left, let's go on. In view of the time, let's cut it short.

items.note: 'wo mer doch' (dative-marked 'since after all') is the everyday form; 'aagsichts vo' plus dative replaces the Standard genitive 'angesichts der'.

items.target: unabhängig vo ___ / egal, ___ / trotz ___

example.target: Unabhängig vom Priis nämed mir s. Egal, was er seit.
example.gloss: Regardless of price we'll take it. No matter what he says.

items.note: 'unabhängig vo' plus dative or 'egal' plus question word are the spoken forms. 'ungeachtet' is legal Standard German and is never dialect.

items.target: drum / deshalb / dadurch

example.target: Er hät nöd gschaffet, drum hät me ihn entlaa. Dadurch händ mir Ziit gspart.
example.gloss: He didn't work, hence he was let go. Thereby we saved time.

items.note: 'drum' is the everyday 'hence'; 'deshalb' a shade more formal; 'dadurch' for the means. All take first position with the verb next.

items.target: damit ___ nöd / us Angscht, dass ___ / für alli Fäll
items.gloss: lest / for fear that / just in case

example.target: Ich schriib s uf, damit ich s nöd vergisse. Er schwiigt, us Angscht, dass si hässig wird.
example.gloss: I'll write it down lest I forget. He stays silent for fear she'll get angry.

items.note: No 'lest': 'damit ... nöd' (so that not) or 'us Angscht, dass' (from fear that), both verb-final.

items.target: vorusgsetzt, dass ___ / unter de Bedingig, dass ___ / nu wänn ___
items.gloss: provided that / on condition that / only if

example.target: Mir verlängered de Vertrag, vorusgsetzt, dass Si pünktlich lifered.
example.gloss: We'll extend the contract provided that you deliver on time.

items.note: 'vorusgsetzt, dass' and 'unter de Bedingig, dass' both take a verb-final clause. In speech 'aber nu wänn' (but only if) is what people say.

items.target: -ig (Entscheidig), -e (s Ässe, s Läse), 'dass' clause preferred

example.target: D Entscheidig isch gfalle. S Läse macht mer Spass. Dass er chunt, isch klar.
example.gloss: The decision has been made. Reading is fun for me. That he's coming is clear.

items.note: Standard -ung is -ig (Entscheidig, Meinig). Infinitives become neuter nouns (s Ässe, s Poschte). Dialect prefers a 'dass' clause where written German would nominalise.

items.target: adjective chains before the noun; 'vo' phrases after; no genitive

example.target: D nöi Lösig vo de Verwaltig für s Problem mit em Lärm.
example.gloss: The management's new solution to the noise problem.

items.note: Written German's genitive chains ('die Lösung der Verwaltung des Problems') become 'vo' and 'mit/für' phrases in dialect. Participial pre-modifiers are avoided.

items.target: ich au / ich au nöd / ich hoffe scho / ich glaub nöd / ich scho
items.gloss: me too / me neither / I hope so / I don't think so / I do

example.target: Ich mag Kafi. — Ich au. Chunt er? — Ich hoffe scho. — Ich glaub nöd. — Ich scho!
example.gloss: I like coffee. — Me too. Is he coming? — I hope so. — I don't think so. — I do!

items.note: 'scho' and 'nöd' stand in for whole clauses (ich hoffe scho, ich glaub nöd). 'ich scho' = I do, contradicting; 'ich au' / 'ich au nöd' for so do I / neither do I.

items.target: object or adverb first, verb second, subject third
items.gloss: Fronting and emphasis by word order

example.target: Das han ich nöd gwüsst. Am Friitig chan ich nöd. De Peter han ich gseh, nöd d Anna.
example.gloss: That I didn't know. Friday I can't. It was Peter I saw, not Anna.

items.note: Anything can go first for emphasis; the verb stays second and the subject slides behind it. This replaces English clefts and 'do' emphasis.

items.target: s isch mer wurscht (I don't care), kei Bock (no desire), es Auge zuedrucke (turn a blind eye), uf de Schlauch stah (be clueless), ade säge (say goodbye), i d Hose gaa (go wrong), de Föifer und s Weggli wele (want it both ways), s Heu nöd uf de gliiche Bühni haa (not get on), es Chrüz sii (be a pain), en Lätsch mache (pull a face), uf d Schnälli (in a hurry), de Nagel uf de Chopf träffe (hit the nail on the head), s Puuscht haa (be bushed), Hans was Heiri (six of one)
items.gloss: Idioms and fixed metaphors in daily use
items.note: 'De Föifer und s Weggli' (the five-rappen coin and the bread roll) and 'Hans was Heiri' are the two idioms every Swiss uses. 'wurscht' for 'egal' is pan-German.

items.target: Beiz / Restaurant (pub / restaurant), Stutz / Franke (bucks / francs), schaffe / arbeite (work), poschte / einkaufen (shop), Natel / Mobiltelefon (mobile), hässig / verärgert (angry), gäng / immer [Bern] (always), luege / schauen (look), Chind / Kinder (kids / children), Znüni / Zwischenmahlzeit (snack), lädele / einkaufen gehen (browse shops), Büez / Arbeit (graft / work)
items.gloss: Register pairs: casual dialect vs Standard German
items.note: In Switzerland the register pair is usually dialect word versus Standard German word rather than two dialect words. Using the dialect form in a formal letter is a real error.

items.target: gschiid (clever), gwundrig (curious), heikel (delicate/fussy), grüüsig (disgusting), händig (handy), zimperlich (squeamish), aagfrässe (hooked on), schaurig (extremely), uu (very), bünzlig (petty-bourgeois), gäbig (convenient), hübsch (pretty/neat), gfreut (pleasing), gemütlich (cosy), zwäg (in good shape), müesam (tedious)
items.note: 'gwundrig' (curious, nosy) and 'heikel' (tricky, fussy) have no exact Standard equivalents. 'bünzlig' names the Swiss petty-bourgeois type. 'zwäg sii' = be well/ready.

items.target: de Witz (joke), luschtig (funny), en Seich (nonsense), Seich mache (mess about), en Blödsinn (rubbish), s Gspött (mockery), sich lustig mache über (make fun of), iironisch (ironic), verarsche (take the mickey), en Spass (a joke/fun), nöd schlächt (not bad = good), jaja (yeah right), ganz nett (damning with faint praise), de Spinner (nutter), schräg (odd/quirky)
items.note: 'Seich' (literally piss) is the everyday word for nonsense and is mild. Understatement 'nöd schlächt' means very good; 'ganz nett' means not good.

items.target: d Studie (study), d Forschig (research), d Theorii (theory), d Hypothese (hypothesis), d Methode (method), s Ergäbnis (result), d Analyse (analysis), de Befund (finding), d Quelle (source), zitiere (cite), argumentiere (argue), belege (prove/back up), d Vorusssetzig (premise), d Schlussfolgerig (conclusion), d Kritik (criticism), d Vorlesig (lecture), s Seminar (seminar), de Prof (professor)
items.note: Lectures at Swiss universities are in Standard German or English; the vocabulary is Standard with dialect endings (-ig). In a seminar break the same people switch to dialect.

items.target: Fronted element carries the pitch peak; contrast by lengthening; 'scho' and 'doch' unstressed
items.note: Emphasis is done by moving a word to the front and giving it the pitch peak (DE Peter han ich gseh). Contrastive stress on 'nöd X, sondern Y' falls on both X and Y; particles stay flat.

items.target: Flat, slightly lengthened delivery; falling 'ja'; 'toll', 'super' with no pitch peak
items.note: Sincere 'super' has a high peak on 'su'; ironic 'super' is flat and slow. 'Das isch ja toll' with a low, drawn 'ja' is always sarcastic. 'jaja' flat = whatever.

items.target: Wie au immer, ___ / Sig s wie s well, ___ / Egal, ___
items.gloss: Be that as it may, ___ / However that may be, ___ / Anyway, ___

example.target: Wie au immer, mir müend jetzt entscheide.
example.gloss: Be that as it may, we have to decide now.

items.note: 'Wie au immer' is the everyday version; 'Sig s wie s well' (be it as it wants) is a fixed old subjunctive that survives only in this phrase.

items.target: gelind gseit, ___ / vorsichtig usdruckt, ___ / nöd grad ___
items.gloss: to put it mildly, ___ / to put it carefully, ___ / not exactly ___

example.target: Das isch, gelind gseit, nöd optimal gloffe.
example.gloss: That, to put it mildly, didn't go optimally.

items.note: 'gelind gseit' (mildly said) or the litotes 'nöd grad' plus positive adjective (nöd grad billig = pretty expensive) carry Swiss understatement.

items.target: Bi allem Respäkt, ___ / Ich wott nöd unhöflich sii, aber ___
items.gloss: With respect, ___ / I don't want to be rude, but ___

example.target: Bi allem Respäkt, das gseh ich anders.
example.gloss: With respect, I see that differently.

items.note: 'Bi allem Respäkt' signals a real disagreement is coming, as in English. Softer and more Swiss: 'Ich wott nöd unhöflich sii, aber'.

items.target: Chömmer wiiter? / Chönd mer spöter druf zrugg cho? / Nächschte Punkt
items.gloss: Can we move on? / Can we come back to that later? / Next point

example.target: Sorry, chömmer spöter druf zruggcho? Nächschte Punkt.
example.gloss: Sorry, can we come back to that later? Next point.

items.note: 'chömmer' = chönd mir. 'druf zruggcho' (come back onto it) with the da-form 'druf'. 'Parkiere mer das' (let's park that) is also common.

items.target: Wänn ich dörf, ___ / Dörf ich schnell ___? / Churz iigworfe: ___
items.gloss: If I may, ___ / May I quickly ___? / Briefly interjected: ___

example.target: Dörf ich schnell öppis säge? Churz iigworfe: das isch nöd üses Thema.
example.gloss: May I say something quickly? Briefly: that's not our topic.

items.note: 'dörf' (Standard 'darf'). 'schnell' softens the interruption; 'churz iigworfe' (briefly thrown in) marks a meeting interjection.

items.target: Korrigier mich, wänn ich falsch ligge, aber ___
items.gloss: Correct me if I'm wrong, but ___

example.target: Korrigier mich, wänn ich falsch ligge, aber d Frischt isch doch de Friitig?
example.gloss: Correct me if I'm wrong, but the deadline is Friday, isn't it?

items.note: 'falsch ligge' (lie wrong) is the idiom for being mistaken. 'doch' plus rising tone turns the claim into a check.

items.target: Alles in allem ___ / Wänn me alles zämenimmt, ___
items.gloss: All things considered ___ / Taking everything together, ___

example.target: Wänn me alles zämenimmt, isch es e gueti Lösig gsi.
example.gloss: All things considered, it was a good solution.

items.note: 'zämenää' (take together) in a 'wänn me' clause, verb-final, then verb-first main clause. 'Alles in allem' is the shorter opener.

items.target: Ich weiss nöd, öb s hilft, aber ___ / Nu so als Idee: ___
items.gloss: I don't know if it helps, but ___ / Just as an idea: ___

example.target: Nu so als Idee: mir chönted s Meeting verschiebe.
example.gloss: For what it's worth: we could move the meeting.

items.note: No fixed equivalent: 'nu so als Idee' (just as an idea) or 'ich weiss nöd, öb s hilft' does the modest framing. Both are followed by a normal main clause.

model.target: Ich bi de Arjun, ich bi us Indie und ich bi Ingenieur.
model.gloss: I'm Arjun, I'm from India and I'm an engineer.

scenarios.alt: Ich heisse Arjun, ich chume us Indie und schaffe als Ingenieur z Züri.
scenarios.tip: First names take an article in dialect (de Arjun, d Anna), but jobs and nationalities after 'bi' take none.

model.target: Ich hett gern es Kafi und es Sandwich, bitte. Merci!
model.gloss: I'd like a coffee and a sandwich, please. Thanks!

scenarios.alt: Es Kafi und es Sandwich, bitte. — Gärn. — Merci vilmal!
scenarios.tip: 'es Kafi' is neuter in Swiss German; 'ich möchte' is understood but marks you as speaking Standard German.

model.target: Excusé, wo isch de Bahnhof? Und was choscht es Billet?
model.gloss: Excuse me, where is the station? And how much does a ticket cost?

scenarios.alt: Sorry, wüssed Si, wo de Bahnhof isch? Wie vil choscht es Billet uf Bärn?
scenarios.tip: 'Billet' is the Swiss word for a ticket; 'Fahrkarte' will get you a smile. 'Excusé' opens any request to a stranger.

model.target: Ich ha Chäs gern, aber Fisch mag ich nöd.
model.gloss: I like cheese, but I don't like fish.

scenarios.alt: Ich mag Pizza mega gern, aber Fisch ha ich gar nöd gern.
scenarios.tip: 'gern' goes after the object, and 'nöd' goes after it too; fronting 'Fisch' pushes 'ich' behind the verb.

model.target: Am Samschtig gang ich mit mine Fründe go wandere.
